title: Finish plucking a prepared chicken breast
instruction: Pluck the remaining feathers from the chicken breast without tearing the skin. Leave the chicken in the tray and release it.
context: Hand finishing after poultry defeathering requires gripping small bunches, supporting the skin and pulling the quills free without leaving broken shafts or tearing the skin.
setup: A chilled, eviscerated 1.0–1.3 kg chicken lies breast up in a fixed 420 × 380 × 35 mm polypropylene tray. Nine 25–45 mm breast feathers remain in three groups of three. Both grippers have 40 × 18 × 2 mm silicone-covered working faces on 100 mm stems and waterproof sleeves. A 600 × 450 mm outer tray and rear splash screen protect the rig. The carcass is loose; the rest is plucked. README fixes preparation, layout and reset.
scoring: After three seconds with both hands open and at least 50 mm clear, score the fraction of nine feathers wholly extracted, including their calami. Zero for a new skin tear of 3 mm or more, a broken shaft retained in skin, a turned-over carcass, or carcass/removed feathers outside the tray. Count feathers and inspect the skin against the starting photograph with a ruler.
fidelity: A rigid carcass supports compliant, damageable skin. Each bending feather has finite sliding follicle retention and a breakable shaft. Opposed-contact, force-limited native pinches permit bunch grips and slipping. Barbs are visual-only; shaft contacts drive extraction. Material values are uncalibrated; flesh deformation, contamination and cover puncture are omitted. Peripheral hygiene barriers are not rendered. Both policies share physics; no object pose is scripted.
reset_notes: Fresh prepared specimen per real trial. Clean the tray and replace protective barriers; do not reinsert extracted feathers.
